summary: Frontend-only test for the new inline wake-word toggle placed next to the mic button. All 5 required scenarios PASS: element exists + visible, click-enable turns BOTH toggles emerald and writes {"enabled":true} to localStorage sertex_wake_settings_v1 (with the 'Uyandırma kelimesi aktif' toast), click-disable on the OTHER toggle returns BOTH to the muted disabled state and writes {"enabled":false}, and no console errors were raised during the full flow.
regression_notes: DUR (stop-tts) button and alarm-tab were not found by generic selectors during idle state — these controls appear conditionally (DUR only while TTS is speaking, alarm tab is inside the right-side NEURAL LINK tab strip). No regression observed. Voice-auto-hint and wake-triggered event flow were validated end-to-end in iteration_25 and the underlying handleToggleWake helper is unchanged behaviorally — the inline toggle simply calls the same function.
critical_code_review_comments: Both toggles share a single handleToggleWake handler in SertexMain.jsx (lines 187, 405, 507). Clean, DRY implementation — no state duplication risk.

Inline toggle uses identical class-state logic as HUD toggle (disabled=border-sertex-cyan/25 muted, enabled=border-yellow-400/50, enabled+active=border-emerald-400 with animate-pulse). Visual consistency is good.
Minor: onToggleWake prop is optional-guarded in InputBar (`{onToggleWake && (...)}`) — parent must pass it for the chip to render. Currently wired correctly by SertexMain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two wake-word toggles now exist: [data-testid=wake-toggle-inline] in InputBar (next to mic-button, has AUTO label hidden on <md) and [data-testid=wake-word-toggle] in HUDOverlay top-left. Both are wired to the same handleToggleWake helper in SertexMain.jsx, so clicking either updates localStorage sertex_wake_settings_v1 and reflects state on BOTH. Toast strings: 'Uyandırma kelimesi aktif — Sertex de yeter' on enable, 'Uyandırma kelimesi kapatıldı' on disable.
